title: T1587.001 — Develop Capabilities - Malware
subtitle: The animation below shows eight steps called "From Code to Compromise".
aria: Animated diagram titled From Code to Compromise. Eight steps show a malware author writing and packing a loader, registering test domains, staging the file, a victim running it, and the SOC responding.

steps.title: Write the loader
steps.caption: The malware author works on an offline virtual machine. The code holds settings, string tables, and the beacon logic. No network connection is needed at this point. Defender signal: nothing is visible. Offline development is invisible by design
steps.defender: Source, CI and artifact logs record who changed what and which artifact was published.

steps.title: Build the binary
steps.caption: A build VM compiles the loader into a working binary. The author strips symbols and sets fake version fields. The output hash is new, so no scanner knows the file. Defender signal: still nothing direct. Build servers sometimes leak artifacts on public code repositories, which researchers later find

steps.title: Test in the lab
steps.caption: The binary runs on a clean test VM. It beacons to a test C2 server to prove the connection logic works. The author watches the traffic and fixes failures. Defender signal: the test C2 domain was registered days ago. Passive DNS partners can spot the new domain early

steps.title: Register test infrastructure
steps.caption: The author registers a new low-cost domain for the test C2 server. Privacy proxy services hide the owner. Domain age is only days. Defender signal: newly registered domains are a cheap early signal. Watch domain age in DNS logs

steps.title: Pack and verify
steps.caption: A packer service compresses and encrypts the binary so scanner tools cannot read its strings. The author checks the result against scanner services until few engines complain. Defender signal: packed first-seen files deserve extra suspicion when they appear later on real endpoints

steps.title: Stage the payload
steps.caption: The packed file lands on a file-sharing platform or a compromised web server. The delivery message will later carry this download link or the file itself. Defender signal: rare executable downloads from code and file platforms are good candidates for hunting (a hunt is a search through stored logs for one indicator)

steps.title: Victim runs it
steps.caption: A victim opens the malicious file. The loader starts, decrypts the payload, and beacons to the production C2 server. The attacker now has a foothold. Defender signal: Sysmon Event ID 1 shows an unsigned first-seen binary. The EDR raises an alert, and DNS shows a rare new domain

steps.title: SOC responds
steps.caption: The SOC isolates the host, saves the sample, and blocks the C2 addresses. Analysts write a short intel note and share indicators with peers. Defender signal: the intel feedback loop. The saved sample improves detection for everyone, including teams that face the same family later
